accent_dynamic_unavailable: Dynamic accent needs Android 12 or newer.
accent_hint: The color of buttons, switches and highlights. Vexel is the signature teal.
align_hint: Select one or more layers - alignment tools will appear here.
blur_hint: Everything under the layer gets blurred. For a frosted-glass look make the fill semi-transparent - the color picker has an alpha slider.
blur_old_android: On Android below 12 the blur only shows in the exported PNG.
code_note: Layout is absolute, like on the canvas. MD3 shapes use MaterialShapes (needs material3 1.4+). Backdrop blur is not exported.
empty_canvas_hint: The sheet is empty. Tap '+' below or long-press the sheet to add a shape.
empty_layers: Nothing here yet. Add a shape with '+'.
eyedrop_hint: Tap the sheet to pick a color
g_back_d: Closes the panel, clears the selection, then returns to projects.
g_dbl_empty_d: Fit the sheet to the screen.
g_dbl_layer_d: Text: edit it; anything else: open Style.
g_drag_d: Moves a layer. Smart guides help you align.
g_handles_d: Corner and side handles resize; the top one rotates.
g_long_layer_d: Select the layer and open Style.
g_panel: Swipe down on a panel header
g_tap_d: Selects a layer. Tapping empty space clears the selection.
g_two_d: Pinch to zoom; move to pan the sheet.
gestures_note: A disabled gesture never fires, so nothing happens by accident. Tap, drag and two-finger zoom can't be turned off - the editor depends on them.
gestures_settings_desc: Turn gestures on or off one by one
glass_ui_desc: Editor panels blur the canvas behind them (Android 12+). Turn off if your phone lags.
guide_add_body: This button opens the menu for adding shapes, text, images, and components. Tap it.
guide_insert_body: Tap one of the tiles in this panel. For example, choose Rectangle to create your first object.
h_editor_start_b: Everything on the white rectangle is a layer. Tap '+' at the bottom, add a shape and drag it. Nothing needs saving, and if you slip up there's the Undo arrow at the top. The three-dot menu has the grid, guides, export and gestures.
h_multi_mode_b: Now every tap adds a layer to the selection or removes it. Once you have the layers you need, open 'Align' or tap 'Group'. Tap the button again to leave the mode.
h_panel_align_b: First select layers (the 'Select' button at the bottom right helps you pick several with taps), then align to the selection or the sheet. Equal spacing needs three layers, same size two.
h_panel_insert_b: Three tabs. 'Basics' - rectangle, ellipse, text, image. 'MD3 shapes' - cookies, bursts, flowers and more, which morph into each other. 'Components' - ready-made buttons, cards, fields. Tap an item to put it on the sheet.
h_panel_layers_b: A list of everything on the sheet. The eye hides a layer, the lock protects it from accidental edits. Groups and components are marked, and their layers can be selected one by one.
h_projects_b: Start with 'New project': a blank sheet or a template, like 'Sign in' or 'Dashboard'. Templates are easy to take apart layer by layer, which makes learning simpler. Language, theme, gestures and tips are in Settings.
h_select_b: The squares at the corners resize, the dot above the layer rotates. The bar at the bottom holds quick actions: duplicate, order, lock, delete. Pull it up to open color, stroke, font and more.
h_select_multi_b: Now you can move them together, group them (button in the bar below) or align them. If they're shapes, 'Combine shapes' is right there: unite, subtract, intersect, exclude.
h_style_blur_b: Shows through a semi-transparent fill: lower the color alpha. Whatever is under the layer gets blurred.
h_style_layer_b: Fill, stroke, opacity, rotation, MD3 corner tokens, text size on the scale, font. If a shape is selected you can change its form - it flows smoothly into the new one.
h_style_project_b: Pick a base color and layers, components and background are recolored by a Material 3 scheme, light or dark. You can take colors from your wallpaper. Canvas size and sheet background are here too.
hints_setting_desc: Short tips the first time you reach a feature
icons_empty_body: Download a Material Symbols set as one file and import it here, no rebuild needed. A .zip or .tgz works: the npm package @material-symbols/svg-400 (on Termux: tools/get_icons.sh) or the google/material-design-icons repository. Import takes a few seconds.
icons_import_failed: No icons found in the archive. Expected a zip or tgz with outlined / rounded / sharp folders
import_unknown_file: Couldn't open that file: it must be a .qwel project or an SVG (up to 2 MB).
label: Label
language_hint: New language: copy en.json from assets/lang, translate the values and add the file with '+ Language' - or just drop it into assets/lang.
language_import_failed: Couldn't add the language: a .json file with translations is required
name: Name
need_storage_permission: Storage permission is needed to save to Pictures/Vexel

tour_0_b:
Top: back arrow, project name (tap to rename), undo and redo, and the three-dot menu - grid, guides, export and gestures live there.
Bottom left: zoom. Tap the percentage to fit the sheet to the screen.
The bottom bar: 'Layers' - everything on the sheet; 'Style' - colors and sizes; '+' - add; 'Align'; 'Select' - pick several layers at once.
When a layer is selected, a bar with quick actions appears above it.
tour_10_b: 'Menu > Compose code' gives you Kotlin: the whole screen or just the selected layers. Tone colors come out as MaterialTheme.colorScheme, MD3 shapes as MaterialShapes, and gradients, shadows and strokes carry over. The layout is absolute, like on the canvas, so it's a good starting point to refine by hand. Backdrop blur isn't exported.\n'Menu > Import SVG' drops someone else's drawing onto the sheet as layers. Rectangles, circles, paths of any complexity, groups and strokes are imported; curves become polylines, while gradients, text and images are skipped, and the app tells you so.
tour_1_b:
Start from scratch and pick a size: phone, compact, tablet, square, desktop or your own. Or take a template and make it yours: sign-in, home, profile, settings, onboarding, product card, 1:1 post, dashboard. Templates are great to take apart layer by layer - it's the fastest way to learn.
Projects can be searched by name and sorted by date, name or size. The three-dot menu on a card: rename, duplicate, PNG to gallery, save as .qwel - a project file that opens on another phone too - or delete.
tour_1_t: A new project: blank sheet or template
tour_2_b:
The '+' button opens three tabs. 'Basics' - rectangle, ellipse, text and an image from your gallery. 'MD3 shapes' - cookies, bursts, flowers, stars, clovers and other Material 3 Expressive forms, the very ones from the loading indicator. 'Components' - ready-made buttons, cards, fields, chips, sliders, dialogs and bottom navigation.
A component isn't a picture but a set of ordinary layers: insert it, tap inside and tweak any detail.
Change a layer's shape and it won't jump - it flows smoothly into the new one.
tour_3_b:
Select a layer and open 'Style': fill, stroke and its width, opacity, rotation, proportions. Rectangle corners come from MD3 tokens (XS to Full), text size from the MD3 type scale, and the font is built-in Figtree or your own .ttf/.otf.
Project tone is the key feature. Pick a base color and the colors of layers, components and background are recolored by a Material 3 scheme, light or dark. You can even take the scheme from your phone's wallpaper (Android 12+).
To change the tone, open 'Style' with nothing selected: canvas size and sheet background are there too.
tour_4_b:
'Select' mode (bottom-right button) picks several layers: tap layers and they join the selection.
In 'Align' first choose relative to what - the selection or the sheet. Then: left, center, right, top, bottom; equal spacing from three layers; same width and height from two; 'Center on sheet' for a single one.
And when you just drag a layer, edges and centers snap to neighbours and guides appear. Toggle it in the three-dot menu.
With several layers selected, handles appear on the corners of the shared frame: drag a corner and all layers scale together, along with corner radii, strokes and font sizes.
tour_5_b:
Select several layers and tap 'Group' - from then on they move together. Tapping an already selected group selects a layer inside it.
'Up' and 'Down' change the order, the lock protects a layer from accidental edits, the eye in the layer list hides it.
'Combine shapes' works like in graphics editors: union, subtract, intersect, exclude. 'Combine' merges outlines into one layer, 'Divide' splits into parts, 'Flatten layers' glues the selection into one image.
Mask: put a shape above an image, select it and tap 'Mask'. The image is cut to the shape, for example a star. A mask only affects the layer directly below it, is not drawn itself and shows as a dashed outline in the editor.
tour_6_b:
The project saves itself after every edit. 'Menu > Export': PNG at 1x to 4x - to the gallery (Pictures/Vexel) or a folder you choose; SVG - clean vector with fonts embedded in the file.
Undo and redo are the buttons at the top, and also two- and three-finger taps. Everything rolls back, even a tone change.
tour_7_b: Every layer has 'Backdrop blur' in Style. It blurs whatever lies under the layer. For a frosted-glass look like Android 17, make the layer fill semi-transparent (alpha slider in the color picker) and add blur.\nOn the canvas it shows on Android 12+; PNG export has it on any Android. SVG has no blur.\nThe editor panels can blur the canvas behind them too. If your phone lags, turn off 'Glass panels' in settings.
tour_8_b: Style has Gradient for shapes: linear with an angle or radial, and the second color is picked like the first. Shadow has blur, offset and color, with presets: soft, raised, glow. The shadow is drawn only outside the shape, so it doesn't show through a glass fill.\nThe eyedropper icon next to the colors turns on a mode: tap anywhere on the sheet and that color goes into the fill, stroke or the gradient's second color.\nGradients and shadows are in PNG and SVG exports too.
tour_9_b: 'Menu > Screens': keep as many same-size screens as you need in one project, such as sign-in, home and settings. Add a blank screen or a copy of the current one, rename and delete them. The title at the top shows which screen is open.\nWhen exporting, turn on 'All screens' and the gallery gets one file per screen. The project tone applies to every screen at once.

tut_done_body:
That's enough for a first screen: open the 'Sign in' template and take it apart layer by layer - it's built from exactly what you just learned.
Tips will appear as you work: one at a time, and only the first time. You can turn them off, like the gestures, in Settings, where you can also replay the tutorial.
tut_dyn_desc: The interface will take its colors from your wallpaper. If you skip it, the signature teal Vexel stays.
tut_look_body: You can change the theme, accent color and font any time in Settings on the main screen. Try it right now, the interface recolors instantly.
tut_quick_add_body: Open '+' to add a shape, text, image, or ready-made component.
tut_quick_move_body: Tap an object to select it, then drag it where you want.
tut_quick_style_body: Select an object and open 'Style'. You can learn extra gestures later in Settings.
tut_s_drag: Now grab it and drag. If another shape is nearby, edges snap to it - those are the smart guides.
tut_s_fit: Flew off somewhere? Double-tap empty space - the sheet fits the screen again.
tut_s_long_empty: Press and hold empty space on the sheet. In the editor this opens 'Add'.
tut_s_long_layer: Press and hold a shape. In the editor this selects the layer and opens 'Style' right away - a shortcut to its settings.
tut_s_pinch: Pinch or spread two fingers - the sheet zooms out or in. Move the same two fingers - the sheet pans.
tut_s_redo: Now three fingers at once - what you undid comes back.
tut_s_tap: To start, just tap any shape on the sheet - that's how a layer is selected.
tut_s_undo: Made a mistake? Quickly tap the sheet with two fingers at once - the last action is undone.
tut_welcome_body:
Vexel is an editor where you draw app screens with your fingers: Material 3 shapes, ready-made components, alignment, export. There's a lot in it, and half of it hides in gestures you can't see on screen.
So first I'll quickly walk you through what's here, then you'll practise on a sample sheet. You do the doing - I only point.
tut_welcome_time: About three minutes. You can stop any time - all of this lives in Settings afterwards.
